content: The guidelines emphasize that some level of enforcement is better than none. They outline fundamental principles and essential components for establishing compliance and enforcement programs, providing examples to guide countries at various stages of implementation. Published in 2006, these guidelines are available in English. The Guidelines for Quality Control of Pesticides provide governments with tools to regulate pesticide quality and prevent the distribution of substandard products. They include guidance on sampling procedures and highlight the responsibilities of governments, industries, and international organizations in quality control programs. The document also addresses legislative, organizational, and resource requirements, as well as regional cooperation, public awareness, and funding. It notes that lowand middle-income countries often face challenges with poor-quality pesticides, leading to ineffective pest control, increased resistance, and health and environmental risks. Published in 2011, these guidelines are available in English, French, Spanish, Russian, and Arabic. The Quality Control of Pesticide Products: Guidelines for National Laboratories assist governments in establishing or enhancing laboratory-based quality control for agricultural and public health pesticides. They cover laboratory organization, staff qualifications, quality assurance, data recording, participation in international studies, and operational procedures. Prepared collaboratively by FAO, WHO, and the Collaborative International Pesticide Analytical Council, these guidelines were published in 2005 and are available in English. The Guidance for Inspection of Pesticide Producers, Importers, Distributors, and Retailers focuses on enforcing compliance through on-site inspections of companies involved in pesticide production and sales. It addresses both chemical and biological pesticides for professional and amateur use. The document provides practical tools, including checklists for inspections and reporting formats for inspectors. It reviews legal frameworks, inspection management, and procedures before, during, and after inspections. Published in 2020, this guidance is available in English. The Guidelines on Pesticide Advertising elaborate on best practices for advertising, as outlined in the International Code of Conduct. They emphasize the role of government authorities in ensuring truthful and responsible advertising. The guidelines cover all pesticide use scenarios and provide a framework for creating legal standards, promoting compliance, and addressing violations. Published in 2010, they are available in English, French, Spanish, and Chinese. The Provisional Guidelines on Tender Procedures for the Procurement of Pesticides advise suppliers and procurers on ensuring good-quality products with appropriate packaging and labeling. They aim to address common issues in lowand middle-income countries, such as substandard formulations and inadequate labeling. These guidelines, prepared in collaboration with the pesticide industry, were published in 1994 and are available in English. The Guidelines for Retail Distribution of Pesticides focus on minimizing risks during storage and handling at supply points, particularly in rural areas. They provide safety instructions, first-aid procedures, and requirements for storage facilities, stock rotation, and record-keeping. The guidelines also address transportation safety and emergency response. Published in 1988, they are available in English. The Guidelines for Procuring Public Health Pesticides promote fairness, transparency, and quality assurance in procurement processes. They assist governments in harmonizing standard operating procedures and cover planning, product selection, legal requirements, and quality control. Published in 2012, these guidelines are available in English. The Guidelines on Good Practice for Ground Application of Pesticides provide comprehensive advice on pesticide application using ground-based equipment. The guidelines also stress record-keeping and monitoring operator health. Published in 2001, they are available in multiple languages, including English, French, Spanish, Russian, Arabic, and Chinese. The Guidelines on Good Practice for Aerial Application of Pesticides focus on safe practices for aerial spraying. They highlight the need for compliance with local regulations, cooperation among stakeholders, and consideration of safety for people, animals, and non-target crops. Published in 2001, these guidelines are available in several languages. They emphasize risk reduction steps, such as using appropriate formulations and avoiding contamination. The guidelines also provide detailed information on selecting and using personal protective equipment (PPE). Published in 2020, they update earlier guidelines and are available in English. The Guidelines on Organization and Operation of Training Schemes and Certification Procedures for Operators of Pesticide Application Equipment outline the importance of training and certification for equipment users. They provide a framework for organizing and sustaining such schemes, emphasizing the need for general knowledge of pesticides and crop protection. Published in 2001, these guidelines are available in multiple languages. The Environmental Management Toolkit for Obsolete Pesticides helps countries plan safe management and disposal programs for obsolete pesticide stocks. It includes methodologies for environmental assessment and risk reduction strategies. Published in 2020, the toolkit is available in English. The Guidelines on Management Options for Empty Containers explain how to design and implement schemes for managing pesticide containers after use. They emphasize decontamination, prevention of inappropriate reuse, and proper disposal. Published in 2008, these guidelines are available in English, French, and Spanish. The Guidelines on Prevention and Management of Pesticide Resistance provide strategies to limit resistance development while protecting crops. They outline practices for resistance management, detection, and prevention, with a focus on agriculture. Published in 2016 and updated in 2018, these guidelines are available in English, French, and Spanish. They provide sample questionnaires and reporting forms and emphasize the importance of data collection and investigation. Published in 2009, these guidelines are available in English, French, and Spanish. They cover monitoring pesticide quality, residues, and accidental poisoning, as well as training and licensing of handlers. Published in 1988, these guidelines are available in English.
